current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (41 FR 37301), as amended by EO 12107 section 2-101 (the Office of Personnel Management substituted for the Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404). The Federal Register document 2026-13154 (91 FR 39361, an OPM final rule published June 30, 2026) still applies the rule as an existing requirement: it states that an individual cannot be admitted to competitive examination or given an appointment in the competitive service unless he or she is a citizen or national of the United States and cites Executive Order 11935 for that rule. reason: The sole paragraph amends Civil Service Rule VII by adding section 7.4 (Citizenship): no person is admitted to competitive examination, and no person is given an appointment in the competitive service, unless a citizen or national of the United States; the Commission may, to the extent permitted by law, authorize the appointment of aliens when necessary to promote the efficiency of the service in specific cases or for temporary appointments. The order carries no sunset, condition or duration. EO 12107 section 2-101 lists EO 11935 under subsection (a) and amends the listed orders by substituting Office of Personnel Management wording for Civil Service Commission wording, effective January 1, 1979; that amendment changes the agency named in paragraph (c) and leaves the rule in force. The held eCFR text of 5 CFR 7.3 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-7.3.txt, not a packet evidence record) reproduces paragraphs (a) to (c) with OPM in place of the Commission under a source note reading E.O. 11935, 41 FR 37301, Sept. 3, 1976, redesignated by E.O. 13197, 66 FR 7853, Jan. 25, 2001. The held text of EO 13197 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_13197.txt, also not a packet evidence record, so it is not attached as a later event) strikes Civil Service Rule VII section 7.2 and redesignates sections 7.3 and 7.4 as 7.2 and 7.3, and its table of sections lists 7.3 Citizenship; it renumbers the section and keeps the rule, so it does not end the clause.
